audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction in this matchup appears nowhere on the page: Goes Where He Pleases makes Dr. Mundo RESIST the first immobilising effect that hits him. Kennen's entire win condition is the three-Mark-of-the-Storm stun, and the first one he lands does not stun — it pops the passive and drops a cannister Mundo can walk over to heal and shorten the passive's own cooldown.
audit.why: Every 'stun-stack + R him' line on the page assumes the stun lands. Against Mundo the first stun is spent breaking the passive, so the reader must plan for a second one or not commit at all. The page instead promises a stun-lock that does not happen.
audit.corrected: report[5].t states it outright, dontsFull[0].d states the cannister heal, tradeGood warns the stun gets eaten first, and breakdown.cooldowns leads with the passive instead of Heart Zapper.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Kennen levels 1 through 5 (rated 8/10 at level 1) on a 45.54% matchup, and phases[0].why claimed 'Q-poke from range wins every melee matchup early' while the content layer's own whys[0] says 'Level 1 is even'. Rows 2-6 were Kennen/Kennen/Skill/Skill/Skill against whys that say he out-trades, out-sustains, heals through your R and out-spikes you.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw out-ranges Kennen's Q — 975 to 950 — on a 4s cooldown and takes a percentage of current health, so a squishy caster cannot win the poke war he is supposed to be winning. The mirror audit already flipped rows 2 through 6 to Dr. Mundo on its side, and the packet levelChart agrees with rows 0 and 2-5.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Kennen / Dr. Mundo / Dr. Mundo / Dr. Mundo / Dr. Mundo / Dr. Mundo in both layers, ratings 5/8/3/3/3/2/2, with phases[0], [2], [3], [4], [5] and [6].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown or range numbers anywhere, on a lane whose whole problem is a 4-second ability that out-ranges yours.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw 4s flat at 975 range, Heart Zapper 17/16.5/16/15.5/15 at 325 range, Blunt Force Trauma 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6, Maximum Dosage a flat 120 — identical to Slicing Maelstrom, so neither side wins the ultimate race.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt; dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and phases[0]/[4].why carry the numbers.

audit.why: The existing anti-heal advice in report[8].t is right and matches the needs-antiheal missing interaction: Heart Zapper heals a percentage of stored damage and Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health. Left as is.

edits.after: Level 1 is even — you chip with one Q, but Infected Bonesaw out-ranges it at 975 and neither of you can commit yet.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heart Zapper's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His stretch: passive regen plus Heart Zapper eats your poke, and nothing you own hard-commits into that. Farm safe and ward.

edits.before: Slicing Maelstrom + Zhonya wins any grouped fight top-side. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s and heals a percent of his missing health mid-storm, then walks you down on his move speed.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heart Zapper's cooldown.
edits.after: Spirit Visage and flat MR turn your first-item burst into chip he simply regenerates back.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: The sidelane is a stalemate you lose alone. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — group, shred MR, and fight with your team.

edits.after: Thundering Shuriken his step-ups and weave an Electrical Surge mark — but count on the stun being eaten first.

notes: The page never once mentioned that Dr. Mundo's passive resists the first immobilising effect. For a champion whose entire win condition is the Mark of the Storm stun, that is the matchup. Now stated in four places. Also fixed: Infected Bonesaw out-ranges Thundering Shuriken (975 vs 950), which is why the 'you out-poke every melee' template line was wrong here. LEVEL CHART / MIRROR DISCREPANCY: the packet levelChart reads row 6 as 'Skill', but the mirror audit on the Dr. Mundo side explicitly flipped its rows 4, 5 and 6 to Dr. Mundo. I followed the mirror so the two directions agree, and row 6 is Dr. Mundo here; if the packet is preferred, rows 6 on both sides need flipping together. Row 1 was left as Kennen — whys[1] and spikes[0] both call it 'your cleanest window' and the mirror did not touch it. The resistances-invalidated missing-interaction was NOT written to the page: Maximum Dosage's percent-health effect is a HEAL, not damage, so 'armour is the wrong answer' does not apply here. diff/diffRating already read TRICKY 7.5/10, consistent with the new chart, so they were left alone.
